report.source_text: Similarly, thrombophilia-related texts showed lower AT III activity (75.1%) and normal AT III antigen level in the father (263.3 mg/L), and MRI showed multiple asymptomatic WMLs (Fig. 1a, b).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old male presented with recurrent bilateral headaches and occasional limb numbness. Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense mutation in the SERPINC1 gene related to antithrombin deficiency (ATD), also found in his father. Biochemical tests showed mildly decreased antithrombin activity with normal antigen levels in both patient and father. Brain MRI demonstrated multiple white matter hyperintensity lesions in both. These findings collectively support a diagnosis of type II hereditary ATD.
